cards.explanation: The answer is imagination, friends. God tells His prophet to say to them, “…out of their own imagination: Hear the word of the LORD!” (Ezekiel 13:2). They're talking up a storm, but the words started in their own heads. That's like me swearing a cookie recipe came from heaven when I dreamed it up during a nap.

The answer is False, and God doesn't dance around it. He says, “Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit yet have seen nothing.” (Ezekiel 13:3). Foolish is the word He uses. Following your own spirit and seeing nothing is not a wisdom plan.

The answer is False, and God says it plainly. “You did not go up to the gaps or restore the wall around the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 13:5). They did not go up to the gaps, and they did not restore the wall. All talk, no trowel.

The wall needed restoring so it would stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD. God says it needed restoring “…so that it would stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD.” (Ezekiel 13:5). It had a job to do on that day. And God says these prophets did not restore it.

The answer is that they wait for it to be fulfilled, friends. The LORD did not send them, “yet they wait for the fulfillment of their message.” (Ezekiel 13:6). They hand out the message and then stand around expecting it to come true. I think that takes some nerve. It's like never turning the oven on and then waiting for the cookies to come out.

What God tells these prophets is, “I am against you.” He says, “Because you have uttered vain words and seen false visions, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.” (Ezekiel 13:8). That's heavy, so I'll say it once and plainly. God takes it seriously when people put their own words in His mouth.

The answer is True. God says they will not “…be recorded in the register of the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 13:9). They also won't belong to the council of His people or enter the land of Israel. That's a lot of doors closing at once.

The word is Peace, friends. God says they led His people astray, “…saying, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace…” (Ezekiel 13:10). The same verse says they were whitewashing any flimsy wall that was built. One soothing word, and there was no peace behind it.
The word is whitewash. God says they were “…whitewashing any flimsy wall that is built…” (Ezekiel 13:10). A fresh coat of white on a weak wall. It looks sturdy right up until the weather shows up.

The answer is False. God says, “…tell those whitewashing the wall that it will fall.” (Ezekiel 13:11). It's not a comfortable message, but it's the true one. A wall that falls doesn't care how nice it looked.

The answer is rain and hail and wind. God says, “Rain will come in torrents, I will send hailstones plunging down, and a windstorm will burst forth.” (Ezekiel 13:11). Three kinds of weather, and one flimsy wall. Paint doesn't hold up in that.

The answer is True. God says, “I will tear down the wall you whitewashed and level it to the ground, so that its foundation is exposed.” (Ezekiel 13:14). Not just cracked, but level to the ground. And all that whitewash goes down with it.

The answer is the city, friends. God says, “The city will fall, and you will be destroyed within it.” (Ezekiel 13:14). It's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to land that way. Then He adds, “Then you will know that I am the LORD.”

The answer is False. God says, “The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it…” (Ezekiel 13:15). He names them as the prophets of Israel who saw a vision of peace for Jerusalem when there was no peace. The wall and the whitewashers are both gone.

The answer is False. God tells His prophet to set his face against these women and says, “Prophesy against them” (Ezekiel 13:17). So the prophet has something to say to them. It starts with “Woe to the women who sew magic charms on their wrists…” (Ezekiel 13:18).

The reason is to ensnare people's souls, friends. These women sew charms and make veils “…in order to ensnare their souls.” (Ezekiel 13:18). The charms and veils are made to trap people. Nothing gentle about it.

The price was handfuls of barley and scraps of bread. God says, “You have profaned Me among My people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread.” (Ezekiel 13:19). Handfuls and scraps. That's a small payment for such a big wrong.

The answer is True, and it's a hard line. God says that by lying to His people who would listen, “…you have killed those who should not have died and spared those who should not have lived.” (Ezekiel 13:19). Their lies pointed life and death the wrong way. I think this one hurts.

God says He'll set them free, friends. He says, “So I will free the souls you have ensnared like birds.” (Ezekiel 13:20). He tears the charms from their arms and the trap opens. Good news after a hard passage.

Righteous goes in the first blank. God says, “Because you have disheartened the righteous with your lies, even though I have caused them no grief…” (Ezekiel 13:22). People who were doing right got discouraged by lies. Wicked goes in the second blank. God says they “…encouraged the wicked not to turn from their evil ways to save their lives…” (Ezekiel 13:22).

The answer is none at all, friends. God says these women disheartened the righteous “…with your lies, even though I have caused them no grief…” (Ezekiel 13:22). The hurt came from the lies, not from Him. He's careful to say so.
